name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,631

clue.text: Up there: some endlessly stormy god

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is lopped off
a storm tosses things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone points at the sky and describes a god raging up above in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up there' feels like a pointer to the heavens, but it is simply raw letters to be mixed with the shortened 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus is the Titan of Greek myth who stole fire for humanity, loosely called a god.

clue.text: Get weight reduced somehow — cook using this

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, so the word loses its final letter
done in some unspecified way, so the letters can come out in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A dieter is told to lose weight one way or another and to cook with a low-fat ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as diet advice; in fact 'Get' and a trimmed 'weight' supply the letters to rearrange. The definition is a loose description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg is a common cooking ingredient, used for meringues and glazes, prized by dieters.

clue.text: Swimmer takes position restricting current

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a place is a position
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A swimmer holds their spot in the water against the pull of the current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person in a race, but it means a fish. 'Current' is electrical, not the flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Urge charming female to go topless

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so losing it means dropping the opening letter

blocks.note: a witch casts charms, so she is a charming female

explanation.surface: Someone urges an attractive woman to go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' is not about attractiveness but about casting charms, that is spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless desire or craving, so it works as a noun synonym for an urge.

clue.text: Meet old man entertaining men say

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside the house, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: 'old man' is slang for one's father
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A man meets his father, who is entertaining some men.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for 'men' is the military abbreviation for other ranks; 'say' signals an example, giving EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To foregather is to assemble or come together, a slightly formal verb synonym for meeting.

clue.text: Location likely to see better girl embracing star

indicators.note: arms embracing someone wrap around them, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A place where a girl hugging a film star might hope to see better things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as the comparative of good, but it means one who bets, a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous for casinos, so it is a spot where gamblers gather in great numbers.

clue.text: Days initially lost in broadcast confused situation

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters are kept
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to beam a programme is to broadcast it
the first letter of the word
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Days of a broadcast are lost amid a muddle at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to both 'Days' and 'lost', not just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum, is a scene of uproar and chaos, a noun synonym for a confused situation.

clue.text: One in flight has tantrums when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: to be in a pet is to be in a sulk or tantrum

explanation.surface: A nervous airline passenger throws tantrums as the plane climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane, but it is a flight of stairs. A pet, in British usage, is a fit of sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a staircase, and each single tread in it is one of its component stairs.

clue.text: Fit pair to be worn by Latvian hunchback

indicators.note: earrings worn by a person hang on either side of the head, so things placed on both sides frame what lies between

blocks.note: to rig out is to fit out or equip
a pair of rings, each ring shaped like the letter O
a Lett is a native of Latvia

explanation.surface: A hunchbacked Latvian is fitted with a pair of something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair is two rings, O and O, worn either side of the Latvian like earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is the hunchbacked court jester who is the title character of Verdi's opera.

clue.text: Worker traps extremely gullible negotiator

indicators.note: a trap closes around its catch, so one piece is held inside another
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: a worker ant, a crossword staple
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A worker outwits a very naive negotiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the insect, the usual crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts and bargains on someone else's behalf, as a sports or literary representative does.

clue.text: Soppy mouth attracting kiss from drunken lips?

blocks.note: a maw is an animal's mouth or jaws
the word as slurred by a drunk, the S blurred into SH

explanation.surface: A sentimental drunk puckers up and slurs a request for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful step: a drunk would slur 'kiss' into 'kish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, and soppy is the informal adjective for exactly that excess of feeling.

clue.text: Obscure English knight against European from the East

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
N is the chess notation for a knight
v. for versus
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: An unknown English knight faces a European opponent from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the knight, but it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap or surround something completely, hiding it from view, as fog does.

clue.text: Worn-out fossil one to throw away

indicators.note: what is sent away is gone, so these letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: a trilobite is a common fossil sea creature
to lob is to throw
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A worn-out old fossil, fit only to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn-out fossil' sounds like one phrase for a tired old person, but the definition stops at the hyphenated adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite describes a phrase or idea overused until stale, which is what worn-out means figuratively.

clue.text: One to march or stroll about in old crown dependency

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
to range is to wander about
the Isle of Man is a British crown dependency

explanation.surface: Someone in a former royal possession chooses between marching and strolling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is a self-governing crown dependency, not part of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Protestant Orange Order in Northern Ireland are known for their annual marching parades.

clue.text: Not prepared for away match

blocks.note: to be off is to be away
to balance is to match or equal

explanation.surface: A football team is unready for its away fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away match' reads as one sporting phrase; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught off-balance means taken by surprise and unready to respond, as a person knocked unsteady would be.

clue.text: Writer's Christmas card impressing bird no end

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is missing
to impress is to press into, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: Noel is Christmas, from the French
taken as written
an owl is a bird; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An author sends a Christmas card with a picture of a bird on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' looks possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was an English playwright, composer and actor, author of Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.

clue.text: Regularly he's in suspect Yemen gallery CIA target

indicators.note: something suspect is not genuine, so the letters are rearranged
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
oft means often, regularly
taken as written
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller picture: a suspect in a Yemeni gallery is on the CIA's hit list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an every-other-letter instruction, but it is a word meaning often. 'Suspect' and 'Yemen' combine, and the Tate is a London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A person deemed a threat to the nation is exactly whom an intelligence agency would hunt down.

clue.text: Freeholders from the Old Country Railway

definitions.note: the answer is a collective noun for the class, the clue a plural

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of 'the'
Oman is a country in Arabia
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Landowners hail from the old country, by way of the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Old' is read together as 'the' in old spelling, not as an adjective for 'Country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were English small farmers owning their own land, and the yeomanry is that class collectively.

clue.text: Sceptical sort acting so atrociously

indicators.note: something done atrociously is badly mangled, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cynical critic reviews a dreadful theatrical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The scathing review is a picture only; the two middle words are the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that the existence of God can be known, a person sceptical in religious matters.

clue.text: Reptile displays pride in Tarsus recklessly

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it
acting recklessly throws things about carelessly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: ego is self-esteem, pride
taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A lizard struts proudly around the ancient city of Tarsus.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarsus, St Paul's birthplace in Turkey, is only fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stegosaur is a plated dinosaur, and dinosaurs are classed as prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: Fur coat owner's hesitant admission?

blocks.note: er is a sound of hesitation
the word an owner uses when claiming a thing as their own
surface padding: frames the two sounds as one confession

explanation.surface: Someone sheepishly admits owning a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fur coat' is the animal's own winter coat, not a garment; the question mark marks the playful wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter pelt of the stoat, used to trim ceremonial robes.

clue.text: Workers organised to run in short jacket

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lost

blocks.note: organised workers form a trade union, abbreviated TU
to run someone in, or nick them, is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Unionised workers are organised to run about in short jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but belongs with 'Workers' as a description. In British slang, to nick someone is to arrest them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket worn as part of a military or police uniform.

clue.text: Jerk outside court with adult signalling of course

indicators.note: lying outside something means going around it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a tic is a jerky involuntary twitch
standard abbreviation
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A fool outside a courtroom with a grown-up, gesturing naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally' but means at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac is the hand-signal code bookmakers once used at British racecourses to pass on changing odds.

clue.text: King needs a wash, mum reflected in capital

indicators.note: a mirror reflection is back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: chess abbreviation
taken as written
waves lap or wash against the shore
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A grubby king is told by his mother to wash, a scene played out in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything after 'King' is read backwards as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the chief city and seat of government of Uganda.

clue.text: Flesh and blood covering fifty pots fired here

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around what it protects, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: one's own flesh and blood are one's relatives
Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Relatives shelter fifty pots that are being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pots fired' hints at gunfire or pot shots, but it is pottery baked in an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is the oven in which potters bake clay vessels hard, the definition describing its function.

clue.text: Dull reporter saying something cutting?

blocks.note: a hack is a mediocre, uninspired journalist
a saw is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: A boring journalist makes a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something cutting' suggests a sharp remark, which fits the surface; the question mark admits it is literally a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, a tool whose whole job is slicing.

clue.text: On radio man would listen

indicators.note: the radio is heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a contraction of 'he would'

explanation.surface: A man on the radio would pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He'd' is the contracted form of 'man would'; the two are spoken identically.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to advice or a warning, a near synonym for listen.

clue.text: Refuse to be carried in this cruise ship?

definitions.text: Refuse to be carried in this

blocks.clueFragment: Refuse to be carried in this
blocks.note: first meaning: a plastic sack fitted inside a dustbin to hold rubbish
second meaning: a large passenger vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline, but it is the noun, rubbish. Refuse is British for household waste, and a bin liner is a rubbish bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a plastic sack lining a dustbin and a big ocean-going passenger vessel.

clue.text: Sound shortened in shout to encourage Maurice?

indicators.note: made shorter means the final letter is trimmed away
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement
a sound argument is a valid one

explanation.surface: A crowd yells encouragement to a performer called Maurice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests noise, which fits the shouting, but it means valid. The definition is by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Chevalier was the French singer and actor of Gigi; the clue defines his surname through his first name.
